_about: The test-links page (test-links.html) reads this list. Every build that gives Karl something to test adds or updates its entries here (see CLAUDE.md, Working with Karl). Each link is the part after the address: it opens the app on that card, level and seed, with sign-in skipped. `level` in a link is the card's saved level number, which can differ from the number on screen (Add to both sides and Divide it: link level 2 is shown as Level 1). `reset: true` clears this browser's progress first. `notLive` says plainly why a link won't work on the live site yet.

groups.title: New: Level 1 is problems, the walkthrough is a button

links.label: Home screen, as a brand-new student
links.look: Hover Solve it. Add to both sides and Divide it both start at Level 1 = their first real problems, with a small “See why it works” button by the dots.

links.label: Reload test
links.look: Hover Solve it, click “See why it works” on Add to both sides, then reload the page: you should land on the home screen, not the walkthrough.

links.label: Add to both sides · Level 1
links.look: The header says Level 1 and the first problem is x + 8 = 11. (This was Level 2 before.)

links.label: Add to both sides · See why it works
links.look: The header says “See why it works” and it’s the numbers-only balance walkthrough. At the end it says “Now you’ve seen why it works!” with a Level 1 button.

links.label: Divide it · Level 1
links.look: The header says Level 1 and the first problem is 3x = 12. (This was Level 2 before.)

links.label: Divide it · See why it works
links.look: The header says “See why it works” and it’s the numbers-only walkthrough.

groups.title: Add to both sides, every level

links.label: Level 1 · x + a = b
links.look: Five problems; the first is x + 8 = 11.

links.label: Level 2 · x − a = b
links.look: Five problems; the first is x − 4 = −3.

links.label: Level 3 · both forms
links.look: A mix; the first is x + 8 = −4.

links.label: Level 4 · x on the right
links.look: Some problems have x on the right side; the first is x + 3 = 10.

links.label: Level 5 · all four forms, bigger
links.look: Everything mixed, bigger numbers; the first is x − 9 = −13.

links.label: Level 1 · a = 2 or 3
links.look: Five problems; the first is 3x = 12.

links.label: Level 2 · a = 2 to 5
links.look: The first is 5x = −15.

links.label: Level 3 · bigger numbers
links.look: Bigger numbers; the first two are 3x = 6 and 2x = 30.

links.label: Level 4 · a = 4 or 6
links.look: The number on x is 4 or 6; the first is 4x = 8.

links.label: Level 5 · all mixed
links.look: Everything mixed; the first is 6x = −18.

groups.title: Lights experiment, Add to both sides (round 1 is now updated to round 2)

links.label: Lights · Level 1 (x + 8 = 11)
links.look: The panel is now narrow: four small moves and round dots. Hover Add for the grey preview, as before.

links.label: Lights · Level 2 (x − 4 = −3)
links.look: The equation reads x − 4 = −3 (it used to say x + −4), and the dashed line runs in front of the =.

links.label: Tucked · Level 2
links.look: One work column with a slim Why? column on the right; Use a move opens a Moves drawer, I’m stuck slides up a counter tray.

groups.title: Add to both sides: help fixes (Build A)

links.label: Partly cancelled: Undo first
links.look: On x + 8 = −4: Use a move, Add −5, Go, then I’m stuck. The line names the +3 that’s left and says to press Undo first, with Undo highlighted.

links.label: A move the wrong way: Undo first
links.look: Use a move, Add 8, Go (it goes red), then I’m stuck: “That move made the equation bigger… press Undo.” After Undo, I’m stuck starts again at the first hint.

links.label: x alone: help with the sum
links.look: On x + 8 = 11: Use a move, Add −8, Go. At x = 11 + −8, press I’m stuck twice: 11 and −8 are outlined and it asks the sum. It never writes the answer, and no seesaw opens.

links.label: x alone: Teach me
links.look: Same as above, but press Teach me at x = 11 + −8: all three sum sentences show and you can type 3 to finish.

links.label: Only two lights judged
links.look: Make the helpful move (Add −8): only Fewer terms and Solved for x change; the other six lights stay dashed.

links.label: Divide it: a fraction that doesn’t split
links.look: On 5x = −15: take ½ of both sides (it fails), then I’m stuck: “That fraction doesn’t split evenly… press Undo.” After Undo, I’m stuck shows the counters.

groups.title: Lights experiment, round 2: the narrow panel (Part A)

links.label: Goals light up on hover
links.look: Hover a round dot: it opens into its goal (“Fewer terms”). On a touch screen, tap it open and tap again to close.

links.label: Forced move after a correct guess
links.look: Type 3 and Check, step through, then Next problem. On the new problem Add has a ring, and x = is grey with “Make one move first.” until you make one move and press Next.

groups.title: Lights experiment, round 2: grab the terms (Part B)

links.label: Drag a number across the line
links.look: Drag “− 4” over the line: it turns into “+ 4 ⇄”. Drop it: the app writes x − 4 + 4 = −3 + 4, then x = −3 + 4, and Fewer terms goes green.

links.label: Combine two numbers
links.look: After the drag above, press Next, then drop the 4 onto the −3. Type a wrong sum (red, it names the sum), then 1 and Enter: a new row x = 1.

links.label: Reorder
links.look: Drag “+ 8” to the left of x: the row becomes 8 + x = 11 in place, no new row, no light changes. Undo puts it back.

links.label: x can’t cross
links.look: Drag x across the line: it snaps back and the line says “That moves x. Try the number.”

links.label: Minus as a negative
links.look: Tap the minus in x − 4: it becomes x + −4 with −4 underlined in purple. Tap that minus again to go back.

links.label: Keyboard only
links.look: Press Tab until “− 4” is outlined, Enter to pick it up, → twice to carry it over the line, Enter to drop. Esc puts it back.

groups.title: Lights experiment, round 2: the Distribute drill (B6)

links.label: Drill: 5 − 2(x + 2) = 3
links.look: Drag the 2 onto the parentheses: it refuses until you tap the minus. Tap it (−2 turns purple), drag −2 onto (x + 2), type −2 and −4 in the labelled blanks, then combine and carry terms until −2x = 2 and type x = −1.

links.label: Drill: keyboard only
links.look: Tab to the 2, press the minus key, then Enter, → (the parentheses go green), Enter: the two product blanks open.

links.label: Drill: 3(x + 1) = 9
links.look: Finish the first problem and press Next problem: 3(x + 1) = 9 has no minus to tap; drag the 3 straight onto the parentheses.
